subject.title: perf(ci): cut the pre-fan-out critical path and bin canonical main runs

question: Should canonical main pushes intentionally spend one Blacksmith preflight runner before the debounce gate in exchange for removing the hosted admission bottleneck and using compact check bins?
rationale: This is an operational CI-capacity and check-contract tradeoff; the supplied patch description is plausible, but the intended main-branch behavior and branch-protection consumers require owner confirmation.

options.title: Validate then merge
options.body: Run and inspect a canonical-main and manual-dispatch workflow to confirm cancellation timing, compact-bin coverage, and release-oriented named checks before merging.

options.title: Keep hosted admission
options.body: Retain the standalone hosted debounce if avoiding any early Blacksmith runner allocation is more important than shortening the main-run critical path.

recommendation.title: Validate then merge
recommendation.body: Run and inspect a canonical-main and manual-dispatch workflow to confirm cancellation timing, compact-bin coverage, and release-oriented named checks before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: This PR's commits and stated performance measurements directly cover the CI topology tradeoff.
